haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, the sweeper sets it EXPIRED and returns the units to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing, no payment is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key, so the provider does not charge twice for the same key.
haiku-low.q4: The claim is refused. The order is cancelled as out of stock, and Payment refunds the full total while the customer gets a cancellation email.
haiku-low.q5: Cart removes checked-out lines only on OrderConfirmed. If checkout fails, the cart is not changed.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service runs the steps in order and records the order's status. Each service records its own state.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a signed webhook to Payment, which writes an outbox event such as PaymentSucceeded that Order reacts to. If no webhook comes, Payment queries the provider.
haiku-low.q8: Payment checks each event id against its processed event ids list. A repeat returns 200 and does nothing. Refund webhooks are deduplicated the same way.
haiku-low.q9: Order moves to FAILED_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the hold. PaymentDeclined triggers this.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory checks that the hold is still HELD and not expired. If so it claims and fulfils; otherwise it refuses and the order is refunded.
haiku-low.q11: Payment retries with backoff and the same key. After a set number of tries it becomes STUCK and pages ops. The refund row is kept in Payment's database.
haiku-low.q12: Cart removes the checked-out lines when OrderConfirmed is published. The Cart service does this.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed, the sweeper sets the reservation to EXPIRED and puts the units back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved (held) before the customer is charged. If any line is short, Inventory writes nothing and returns the short items; the order becomes FAILED_SHORT_STOCK, no payment is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) sent with the charge request; with the same key the provider does not charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Inventory refuses the claim; the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is refunded in full (Payment refund requested) and emailed about the cancellation.
sonnet.q5: The cart is cleared only when the order is confirmed (on OrderConfirmed, Cart removes the checked-out lines; lines added after the snapshot stay). If checkout fails, the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q6: The Order service drives the steps; the order's status is recorded in the Order service (its own database, e.g. PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to the Payment service (after checking its signature, Payment records it and writes an outbox row); Payment publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as an event on the broker, and Order reacts to it. If no webhook comes within 30 minutes, Payment queries the provider and treats the answer as a webhook.
sonnet.q8: Payment checks the webhook's event id against its processed event ids; if already recorded it returns 200 and does nothing. New events are recorded in the same DB transaction as the state change.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released (reservation set RELEASED, units back on sale). Triggered by Order, which on PaymentDeclined moves to FAILED_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release.
sonnet.q10: At claim time Inventory checks whether the reservation is still HELD and not expired. If yes, it is CLAIMED and the order is confirmed; if not (late success), the claim is refused and the order is cancelled with a full refund.
sonnet.q11: Payment retries with backoff using the same key. After a set number of tries (number not stated) the refund becomes STUCK, operations are paged, and the row is kept until resolved. It is tracked as a refund row in Payment's database (REQUESTED, then REFUNDED or STUCK).
sonnet.q12: Order's OrderConfirmed event causes it; the Cart service removes the checked-out lines.
